correctness.rationale: Use the closed neighborhoods in RESULT.md lines 56–69; non-codeword traces must be nonempty and pairwise incomparable because the difference condition applies to both orders. If x is absent, any absent v_i has trace inside I_C(x), so all v_i are present. With y present the remaining outsider traces are the distinct singletons {v_i}, incomparable with I_C(x), which contains y but no v_i. Interchanging the sides handles y absent and x present. If both spines are absent the same forcing gives all page vertices, and the two outsider traces U and V are disjoint and nonempty since m≥1. If both spines are present an empty page gives traces {x} and {y}, which prohibit any other outsider. Without an empty page every outsider has a two-element trace containing the corresponding spine and a selected page mate. These traces are distinct, hence incomparable. The disjoint contributions are 2z^(m+1)(1+z)^m from one spine, z^(2m) from neither, mz^(2m) from an empty page with both spines, and z²(2z+z²)^m from both spines and no empty page. The lowest power is m+1; at m=1 the z^(2m) contributions tie and there are four minima, while for m≥2 only the two one-spine choices of lowest size qualify. At z=1 the stated total follows. The frozen checker and output were inspected, not executed; they compare actual masks and coefficients on 349,520 subsets through m=8 only. The trace argument, including sufficiency in each branch, proves the all-m result.

value.rationale: The family is a natural non-ladder prism and shared-edge cycle book. Its full code-size spectrum and actual choices are useful beyond the scalar minimum bound. In particular, the exact rule that emptying one page forces every other page to be full produces a distinct coefficient contribution; it is a structural constraint, not a sampled count or a rescaled existing invariant. The result also accounts for the transition from four minimum codes on the square to two rigid minima on larger books.
